title: Out of One, Many: Using Language Models to Simulate Human Samples
measurement_description: The paper measured the model's ability to replicate human stereotypes and correlations related to religion in the context of US politics. This included generating descriptive stereotypes associated with religious labels (e.g., 'Christian', 'Atheist') for political partisans and accurately modeling the correlation between religious practice (i.e., church attendance) and political behaviors like voting choice and other demographic/attitudinal variables.
findings: GPT-3 demonstrated a high degree of 'algorithmic fidelity' in relation to religious data within the US political context. The model successfully replicated human-like stereotypes, associating 'Christian' with Republicans and 'Atheist' with Democrats. Furthermore, it accurately modeled the strong correlation found in human populations between religious practice (church attendance) and political behaviors, such as presidential vote choice, and other attitudes.
